a1.label: 1. Why 13:00 CET?
a1.why: The text says the time is early enough for Brazil and late enough for India, suiting all three offices.

a2.label: 2. Why keep calendars updated?
a2.why: The text says this lets colleagues see when you are available.

a3.label: 3. If your connection is weak, you should...
a3.why: The text says to turn the camera off and say your name before speaking.

a4.label: 4. According to Priya, direct feedback...
a4.why: The text says direct feedback can sound harsh to colleagues from other cultures.

a5.label: 5. Priya recommends...
a5.why: The text says to ask questions instead of making statements.

a6.label: 6. The kick-off takes place...
a6.why: The text says the kick-off is on Monday.

b1.label: 1. India and Germany are in different ___
b1.why: India and Germany are in different time zones.

b2.label: 2. Anyone with an interest in project success
b2.why: A ‘stakeholder’ is anyone with an interest in the project's success.

b3.label: 3. Must deliver by Friday — a hard ___
b3.why: A firm delivery date is called a hard deadline.

b4.label: 4. Works without sharing a physical office
b4.why: A ‘remote team’ works together without sharing a physical office.

b5.label: 5. Understanding how other cultures communicate
b5.why: ‘Cultural sensitivity’ is understanding how other cultures communicate.

b6.label: 6. A one-hour ___ with Dublin
b6.why: A one-hour video call is a meeting over video.

b7.label: 7. Conferences build your ___
b7.why: Conferences are a good place to build your professional network.

c1.label: 1. Could you tell me when the meeting ___?
c1.why: Indirect questions keep normal word order — no ‘does’.

c2.label: 2. I was wondering if you ___ the report yet

c3.label: 3. Do you know ___ the server is located?
c3.why: ‘Where’ asks about location, with normal word order in the indirect question.

c4.label: 4. Could you explain how ___?
c4.why: Indirect questions keep normal word order — no ‘does’.

c5.label: 5. Would you mind ___ the document again?
c5.why: ‘Would you mind’ is followed by the gerund (-ing) form.

c6.label: 6. May I ask why ___ delayed?
c6.why: Indirect questions keep normal word order — no ‘was the release’.

c7.label: 7. I'd like to know whether the update ___ tested
c7.why: The passive present perfect ‘has been tested’ agrees with singular ‘the update’.
